questions.question: An official enumeration of population done periodically is known as:
questions.questionHtml: An official enumeration of population done periodically is known as:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is census.

Key Points

  • A census is a periodic official enumeration of the population.
  • The first census in India was conducted in 1872. However, the first complete census was done in 1881.
  • Since then, every ten years, censuses have been held. The most thorough source of demographic, social, and economic statistics is the Indian Census.
  • The Registrar General and Census Commissioner of India, under the Ministry of Home Affairs, conducts a census every ten years.
  • In 2021, India will conduct its 16th census.
  • Union Home Minister Amit Shah announced in September 2019 that the 2021 national census would be conducted entirely digitally via a mobile phone application. 

Important Points

  • Any statistical component that influences population growth or decline can be included in demographics, although six characteristics are particularly important: population size, density, age structure, fecundity (birth rates), mortality (death rates), and sex ratio (Dodge 2006). 
  • The Citizenship Act of 1955 was amended in 2003, requiring the development of the National Register of Citizens (NRC). Its goal is to identify and expel illegal immigrants by documenting all legal citizens of India.
  • The National Population Register (NPR) is a database of people who live in a hamlet, rural region, town, ward, or delimited area within a ward in a city or town.

questions.solution: The correct answer is 1921. Great Divide in the demographic history of IndiaThe year 1921 is taken as the demographic divide for the reason that before this year, the population was not stable, sometimes it increased and at other times it decreased.  ​Prior to 1921, the course of population growth was undulating (several ups and downs, mainly because of mortality differentials).

questions.question: In how many phases was the 2011 Census conducted in India?
questions.questionHtml: In how many phases was the 2011 Census conducted in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Two.

Key Points

  • The 2011 Census of India was conducted in two distinct phases.
  • The first phase, known as the House listing and Housing Census, took place from April to September 2010.
  • The second phase, Population Enumeration, was conducted from 9th to 28th February 2011, with a revision round from 1st to 5th March 2011.
  • The Census was carried out by the Office of the Registrar General and Census Commissioner, India, under the Ministry of Home Affairs.
  • It was the 15th National Census of the country since 1872.

Additional Information

  • House Listing Phase:
    • This phase involved the listing of all houses, whether occupied or vacant, and collecting information on the amenities available to the households.
    • It also included a National Population Register (NPR) for the biometric details of residents.
  • Population Enumeration Phase:
    • This phase recorded demographic details of the individuals such as name, age, sex, religion, and occupation.
    • Special provisions were made to include homeless populations and those living in institutions.
  • National Population Register (NPR):
    • The NPR was created to have a comprehensive identity database of residents.
    • It includes demographic and biometric data of individuals.
  • Technology Use:
    • For the first time, the 2011 Census used modern technology like GIS and GPS for mapping and data collection.
    • Data processing was done using advanced software to ensure accuracy and speed.

  • Population enumeration is the phase 2 processes in a census after House listing and Housing Census.
    • During the 2011 census process, the population enumeration was conducted from 9th February to 28th February 2011.
    • The government will collect a set of demographic, social and economic data on every person in the country by population enumeration.
    • There were 29 questions canvassed during population enumeration in the Census of 2011.
    • To collect information on more than 120 crore people in just 20 days, the government called on government employees to participate as enumerators.
    • Teachers were the main source of enumerators.

Additional Information

  • A population Census is a process of collecting, compiling, analyzing and disseminating demographic, social, cultural and economic data relating to all persons in the country, at a particular time in ten years interval. 
  • The Census of 2011 was the 7th number after the Independence and 15th edition when counted from 1872.
  • The first Census in India was conducted in 1872 during the British period.
  • The first Census of Independent India was conducted in 1951.
  • The first phase House listing and Housing Census has been conducted between April to June 2010 in different States and UTs.
    • The House listing and Housing Census of 2011 contains 34 questions.

questions.solution: A 'marginal worker' as defined by the Census of India is an individual who works for less than 183 days (or six months) in a year. These workers are typically engaged in seasonal, irregular, or part-time employment. They often work in sectors such as agriculture, labor, or other informal industries where employment is not continuous throughout the year. In contrast, 'main workers' are those who work for 183 days or more during the year.

questions.question: Infant Mortality Rate (or IMR) indicates the number of children that die before the age of ______ as a proportion of 1000 live children born in that particular year.
questions.questionHtml: Infant Mortality Rate (or IMR) indicates the number of children that die before the age of ______ as a proportion of 1000 live children born in that particular year.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 1 year.

Key Points

  • Infant mortality rate
    • It is the probability of a child born in a specific year or period dying before reaching the age of one if subject to age-specific mortality rates of that period. Hence, Option 3 is correct.
    • The infant mortality rate is strictly speaking not a rate (i.e. the number of deaths divided by the number of population at risk during a certain period of time) but a probability of death derived from a life table and expressed as a rate per 1000 live births.
    • In accordance with the UN Millenium Development Goals (MDG), the goal was to cut down child mortality rate by two-thirds from 1995 to 2015.

Additional Information

  • In India, it declined considerably at the rate of almost 57%. The IMR came down from 80 infant deaths per 1000 live births (in 1995) to 33 deaths per 1,000 live births (in 2017: according to the SRS bulletin 2019).
  • IMR has 2 components:
    • IMR: infants dying within 1 year of birth and,
    • Neonatal Mortality Rate (NMR): It is defined as the ‘number of deaths during the first 28 completed days of life per 1,000 live births in a given year or period’.
  • Globally according to UNICEF, NMR was 18 deaths per 1000 live births (in 2018), whereas, in India, NMR was 23 deaths per 1000 live births (approximately 7,000 newborn deaths every day).
  • The decline in NMR is at a very slow pace both globally and in India. It is almost one-third of the rate of decline of IMR.

questions.question: As per Census 2011, which of the following northern states has the highest literacy rate?

questions.solution: As per Census 2011, Himachal Pradesh recorded the highest literacy rate among northern states at 82.80%. questions.question: The decennial Census is conducted by the Office of the Registrar General and Census Commissioner belonging to which ministry?
questions.questionHtml: The decennial Census is conducted by the Office of the Registrar General and Census Commissioner belonging to which ministry?

options.text: Ministry of Statistics and Program Implementation
options.html: Ministry of Statistics and Program Implementation

questions.solution: The decennial Census in India is conducted by the Office of the Registrar General and Census Commissioner under the Ministry of Home Affairs. Conducted under the Census Act of 1948, the responsibility of this Union subject is outlined in Article 246 and serial number 69 of the Seventh Schedule of the Constitution. Census data is vital for determining political representation, resource allocation, and the proportion of reserved legislative seats for SC and ST populations. The last Census was in 2011, noting a population of 1.21 billion, a literacy rate of 74.04%, and a sex ratio of 940 females per 1,000 males.

questions.question: According to the Census 2011 of India, which metropolitan has the second highest population?
questions.questionHtml: According to the Census 2011 of India, which metropolitan has the second highest population?
questions.solution: According to the 2011 Census of India, Delhi had the second highest metropolitan population of approximately 16.8 million, following Mumbai with around 20.4 million. Kolkata was the third largest with about 14.1 million. The total population of India was approximately 1.21 billion, with a growth rate of 17.7% from the previous decade. The overall sex ratio was 940 females for every 1,000 males. Urban population constituted 31.16%, while rural was 68.84%. The national literacy rate was 74.04%, with Kerala having the highest literacy rate at 93.91% and Bihar the lowest at 61.80%.

questions.question: Officially, the first recorded statistics on transgenders were collected in which census in India?
questions.questionHtml: Officially, the first recorded statistics on transgenders were collected in which census in India?
questions.solution: India officially recorded transgender statistics in the 2011 Census. It marked the 15th Census of India, estimating the population at 1.21 billion. It highlighted key figures like literacy rate (74%), sex ratio (943), and child sex ratio (918). Conducted in two phases, it followed the 1948 Census Act under Article 246.

questions.question: What is density of population in NCT of Delhi as per the 2011 Census?
questions.questionHtml: What is density of population in NCT of Delhi as per the 2011 Census?
questions.solution: The 2011 Census recorded the population density of the National Capital Territory (NCT) of Delhi as 11,320 people per square kilometer, making it one of India's most densely populated regions. This high density highlights Delhi's importance as a major urban and capital city. The population density data is crucial for urban planning, infrastructure development, and resource allocation. It helps address challenges like traffic congestion, pollution, and housing. Regular census data, collected every ten years, provides essential demographic insights for effective governance and policy-making in metropolitan areas.
